Mode B — derive: with no debt drawn under $30M JPM revolver and $41.1M operating cash flow, this is a NET CASH issuer ($257M cash vs $52M total liabilities ex-deferred comp). rfm_tuples.M_source: FY2023 10-K balance sheet + Q1'24 10-Q balance sheet (acc 0001628280-24-020035) + Cash Flow Statement
rfm_tuples.M_value: VERIFIED. Cash $257.2M (FY23) -> $249.4M (Q1'24, -$7.8M Q/Q burn driven by working capital). Zero drawn debt. $30M JPM revolver undrawn. Operating CF +$41.1M (FY23) vs +$31.7M (FY22). In compliance with all covenants (consolidated total leverage ratio) per both 10-K and Q1'24 10-Q. Total stockholders equity $382.9M. No going-concern, no substantial-doubt language, no covenant amendment. Q1'24 cash burn is concerning but absolute balance gives ~30+ quarters of runway at that pace.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Capital structure claim is fully supported. GDYN is the OPPOSITE of a credit-distressed small-cap — net cash, profitable on operating-CF basis, no covenant pressure. rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify customer-count and concentration tables. Mode B — Derive Q1'24 forward trajectory by reading the next 10-Q (filed 2024-05-02, pre-cutoff): is the 'comparable' narrative still intact one quarter later?
rfm_tuples.M_source: FY2023 10-K MD&A customer-concentration table + Q1'24 10-Q MD&A customer-concentration table
rfm_tuples.M_value: CLAIM EVOLUTION RED FLAG. FY2023: 275 customers (up 1.1% from 272). Q1'24 10-Q (filed 2024-05-02): 'the total number of customers was 210, down from 220 customers in the same period a year ago' — a 4.5% YoY DECLINE in active customer base, the first contraction visible in the dataset. Concurrent top-one customer concentration rose Q1'24 to 16.7% (vs 13.9% Q1'23 and 14.4% FY23) — a +280 bps single-customer concentration jump in one quarter. CPG/Manufacturing vertical revenue -24.4% YoY in Q1'24. Trajectory: Q1'23 220 -> Q2'23 247 -> Q3'23 265 -> FY23 275 -> Q1'24 210 (these are period-cumulative counts so the right comparison is 220 -> 210). Either way, the FY23 'comparable' framing is no longer operative one quarter later.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: FY2023 10-K presented customer base as stable. Q1'24 10-Q (still pre-cutoff) discloses a customer-count contraction and rising top-one concentration — a classic IT-services demand-rollover signal. Not a lie (Q1'24 honestly disclosed) but the FY23 framing of stability has been falsified within ten weeks. Forward demand quality is the dominant uncertainty for GDYN.

rfm_tuples.R: 'We recorded revenues of $312.9 million, an increase of $2.4 million, or 0.8% from the previous year.' (FY2023 10-K, vs $310.5M in 2022 and $211.3M in 2021 = +47% in 2022).
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify revenue magnitude against income statement and vertical disaggregation. Mode B — Compute deceleration: +47% (2022) -> +0.8% (2023) -> Q1'24 flat YoY ($79.8M vs $80.1M = -0.3%). How does management frame the deceleration?
rfm_tuples.M_source: FY2023 10-K Income Statement + Q1'24 10-Q Income Statement + revenue-by-vertical disaggregation
rfm_tuples.M_value: Revenue growth collapsed from +47.0% (2022) to +0.8% (2023) to -0.3% (Q1'24 YoY). CPG/Manufacturing vertical fell from $61.2M (2022) to $42.9M (2023, -30%) and continued to -24.4% YoY in Q1'24. Retail (32.8% of mix) grew only 2.9% in 2023. Gross margin compressed 38.8% (2022) -> 36.2% (2023) -> 34.7% GAAP (Q1'24) — 410 bps cumulative compression. Loss from operations $5.6M (2023), $5.5M (Q1'24). FY23 10-K MD&A explanation: 'gross profit margin ... was driven by a combination of increased personnel costs and foreign exchange effect' — single-line, no quantification of bench utilization, no T&M billable-hour disclosure even though the business uses utilization as a key metric.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Revenue deceleration from 47% to ~0% is the single biggest business story, but the MD&A devotes one sentence to gross-margin explanation. No disclosure of bench utilization rate, no headcount-trajectory table, no FX quantification despite citing it. The 0.8% growth print is honest, but the framing buries the magnitude of the macro/IT-services slowdown. Mode-B: a name that earns $115M cash-gross-profit and reinvests via SBC of $35M is in services-margin-compression territory, not growth territory.

rfm_tuples.R: 'Total stock-based compensation $35,516 ... $60,968 ... $33,036' (FY23, FY22, FY21 — in $thousands; 10-K Note 11). 'We managed to decrease net loss by 94.0% to $1.8 million due to lower levels of operating expenses.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify SBC magnitude relative to revenue and net loss. Mode B — derive: GAAP net loss of $1.8M while SBC was $35.5M means cash-economic loss before SBC was $33.7M positive but per-share dilution is large. Compare Non-GAAP EBITDA framing.
rfm_tuples.M_source: FY2023 10-K Note 11 + Income Statement + Non-GAAP reconciliation in MD&A
rfm_tuples.M_value: SBC = $35.5M on revenue of $312.9M = 11.4% of revenue. Net loss = $1.8M GAAP. SBC was 20x larger than the reported net loss, meaning the 94% net-loss improvement narrative is mathematically a reduction of SBC dilution rather than an operating improvement. Non-GAAP EBITDA of $44.2M (14.1% margin) excludes the $35.5M SBC; if SBC were treated as a cash compensation expense (which it is, economically), Non-GAAP EBITDA falls to ~$8.7M (~2.8% margin). Share count rose from ~74.5M (Q1'23 weighted) to ~76.2M (Q1'24 weighted) = +2.3% dilution YoY. Annual share dilution rate roughly matches the entire 'net loss improvement.'
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Non-GAAP EBITDA framing relies on SBC add-back of $35.5M = 11.4% of revenue, well above peer norms (5-7% typical for offshore IT services). The headline 'reduced net loss 94%' is technically true but is a function of declining SBC ($61M -> $36M, partly because outsize 2022 RSU/PSU vest cliff has passed) rather than operating improvement. Mode-B observation: a $1.8M GAAP net loss masked by $35.5M of dilutive comp is an honesty-of-profitability concern but not a lying-detector hit.

rfm_tuples.R: 'No director or officer, as defined in Rule 16a-1(f), adopted or terminated a Rule 10b5-1 trading arrangement or a non-Rule 10b5-1 trading arrangement, as defined in Regulation S-K Item 408, during the three months ended March 31, 2024.' (Q1'24 10-Q Item 5)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify against EDGAR Form 4 filings during the same period to check for systematic insider sales that would imply a pre-existing plan. Mode B — derive: if no plan was adopted but the CEO is selling in monthly cadence at consistent share counts, either an undisclosed pre-existing 10b5-1 exists or sales are discretionary during a -26% drawdown.
rfm_tuples.M_source: EDGAR Form 4 filings 2024-01-01 to 2024-05-15 (59 filings in 12 months pre-cutoff) — raw XML reportingOwner + transactionCode parsed
rfm_tuples.M_value: PATTERN CONFIRMED. CEO Leonard Livschitz executed code-S (open-market sale) Form 4 transactions on the following dates (sample, all pre-cutoff, all under code S not code F tax-withholding): Jan-31 (15,000 sh @ $13.06), Feb-15 (15,000 @ $13.08), Feb-29 (15,000 @ $13.88), Mar-13 (15,000 @ $12.36), Mar-27 (15,000 @ $12.03), Apr-11 (15,000 @ $11.87), Apr-24 (10,000 @ $10.54), May-09 (10,000 @ $10.68). That is roughly 110,000 shares sold by the CEO Jan-May 2024 totaling ~$1.4M of proceeds AT FALLING PRICES (from $13.88 down to $10.54) during the 26% drawdown. CFO Anil Doradla executed parallel code-S sales (3-4k shares roughly every 2 weeks). Pattern is mechanically rhythmic (Wednesdays, similar share counts) — consistent with a pre-existing 10b5-1 plan, but the Q1'24 10-Q affirmatively states no plan was adopted/terminated in Q1, which only means the plan (if any) was adopted in a prior quarter and the company has provided no plan-adoption-date disclosure that the framework can verify.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode-B finding: Item 408 disclosure as written is technically compliant (no plan adopted/terminated IN the quarter), but the absence of any plan-adoption-date disclosure for what is functionally a programmatic sales pattern is a transparency gap. CEO selling steadily into a -26% drawdown is also incompatible with a strong insider-conviction read; either insiders see the demand softness reflected in Q1'24 customer counts (C2) or they are wealth-diversifying mechanically. Not a SEVERE signal because the math is small relative to CEO compensation, but framework-relevant.

rfm_tuples.R: Goodwill = $53.9M (Dec-31-2023) vs $45.5M (Dec-31-2022); Intangible assets net = $26.5M vs $20.4M. Three named acquisitions in disclosure (NextSphere Apr-2023, Mutual Mobile Dec-2022, Tacit Knowledge May-2021). NextSphere acquired during 2023.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify goodwill increase reconciles to NextSphere purchase price and that no impairment was recorded. Mode B — derive: with three sub-scale acquisitions adding ~$54M goodwill on a company with $5.6M operating LOSS, what is the implied goodwill-impairment risk under ASC 350?
rfm_tuples.M_source: FY2023 10-K Note 4 (Acquisitions) + Note 6 (Goodwill) + Balance Sheet + MD&A
rfm_tuples.M_value: Goodwill grew $8.4M from NextSphere (Apr-2023) acquisition. No impairment recorded. Cumulative acquired-business contribution to revenue is not disclosed by segment. The Company has only one reportable segment so goodwill is tested at the entity level — and entity-level fair value (market cap ~$80M at cutoff implied by $10.54 share price × 76M shares = ~$800M; well above book equity of $383M) provides headroom. So even at the -26% drawdown share price, market cap is 2x book equity and 15x goodwill, so no triggering event for impairment exists yet. Mode-B caveat: NextSphere and Mutual Mobile each added ~180 employees and modest revenue — these are talent-acquisitions, and if the cohort consolidates, goodwill at ~12% of total assets is modest.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Goodwill is well-supported by current market cap even after drawdown. Acquisition strategy is small-bolt-on, not transformational, so the impairment risk is low. Counterweight to C2's customer-count concerns.

rfm_tuples.M_source: FY2023 10-K Note 7 (Debt) + Q1'24 10-Q + 8-K lookback for amendments
rfm_tuples.M_value: JPM revolver ($30M capacity) original date March 15, 2022; no amendment filings in EDGAR 8-K lookback (no 8-K Item 1.01 amendment-of-material-agreement filings related to credit facility between 2022-03-15 and cutoff). $0 drawn at both year-end 2023 and Q1'24. Facility used solely as a backstop. Consolidated total leverage ratio covenant is the only financial covenant; with $0 drawn it is trivially satisfied. This is the OPPOSITE of the AAP-style covenant-amendment distress signature that the framework is calibrated to find.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Clean credit profile: zero drawn debt, no amendments in 2 years, one trivial financial covenant. This is a strong positive signal that distinguishes GDYN from credit-distressed names in the cohort.

summary: GDYN is a $313M-revenue offshore digital-engineering services firm with a fundamentally clean balance sheet — $257M cash, zero drawn debt, positive operating cash flow ($41M FY23), Big-4-adjacent auditor (Grant Thornton) with seven-year clean tenure, no going-concern language, no material weakness, no covenant amendments, no late filings, no critical audit matters. The -26.2% pre-cutoff drawdown is not a solvency or fraud-detection problem but a demand-rollover problem visible in the claim evolution between the FY2023 10-K (filed 2024-02-29) and the Q1'24 10-Q (filed 2024-05-02): customer count contracted from FY23's '275 ~ comparable to 272' framing to '210, down from 220' in Q1'24, top-one customer concentration jumped 230 bps in one quarter, gross margin compressed another 150 bps to 34.7%, and revenue inflected from +0.8% to -0.3% YoY. CEO and CFO ran a programmatic open-market sales pattern (~$1.4M of CEO proceeds Jan-May 2024 at descending prices from $13.88 to $10.54) while the company asserts Item 408 compliance without disclosing the plan-adoption dates — a transparency gap. SBC at 11.4% of revenue masks GAAP near-breakeven through dilution rather than operating improvement. Verdict: NEUTRAL with a tilt to LONG — distress framework finds no liars and no covenant/solvency catalysts (5 PASS, 4 MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY, 1 UNVERIFIABLE, 0 SEVERE, 0 RED_FLAG), but the customer-base contraction is real and the insider sales suggest at least mild internal concern about near-term demand. This is the framework's intended discrimination: a drawdown name that is NOT lying.
